title: Chicken drumstick, stewed, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks are the meat from the thigh portion of a chicken, commonly prepared as stewed dishes. The skin is removed and not consumed, which reduces the fat content. Stewing keeps the meat tender, infuses it with spices, and preserves valuable nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks are a staple in many world cuisines, from Russian to Asian recipes.
Stewing retains more B‑vitamins compared with frying.
The thigh meat contains a good amount of collagen found in connective tissue.
Removing the skin sharply lowers saturated fat levels.
Stewed drumsticks keep well in the fridge for 3‑4 days or can be frozen for longer storage.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Drumsticks provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain B1, B2, B3, B6 and B12, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health, blood formation, and wound healing.

items.title: Low fat when skin is removed
items.content: Without the skin, the calorie and saturated‑fat content is reduced, benefiting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: A rich amino‑acid profile helps maintain and build muscle, especially for active individuals.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked or improperly stored meat can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter.

items.title: Sodium in prepared dishes
items.content: Stewed drumsticks are often seasoned with salt and sauces, increasing sodium intake.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: People with gout should monitor consumption as it may trigger attacks.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stewed drumsticks can be served as a main course, added to soups, stews, salads, or used as a filling for pies. When serving, it is advisable to remove bones and any small cartilage fragments.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked drumsticks in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.
